rows.description: Family WhatsApp groups turn every festival into a political fight. You may love them and still be exhausted by forwards. Set gentle rules: no forwards, verify before sharing, change the subject warmly, or mute without drama.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, admiration, anger, contempt, loyalty
related mind states: affection, tiredness

rows.description: A close friend has opposing views, and you wonder if the friendship can survive. Decide which values truly matter, talk openly when it is about dignity, and let differences on policy coexist with care if respect remains.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, admiration, anger, argument, contempt
related mind states: admiration, curiosity, awe

rows.description: You admire a leader and feel part of a cause. Support can be sincere, but keep the ability to criticise. Treating leaders as infallible turns citizens into followers, and disagreement on specific acts is not betrayal.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, argument, contempt, loyalty
related mind states: admiration

rows.description: Volunteering for a movement gives energy and friends. Good: canvassing honestly, listening to voters, and knowing your limits. Watch for slogans replacing thinking and for excusing your side's wrongs.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, anger, argument, contempt, loyalty
related mind states: nostalgia

rows.description: Voting, paying taxes, attending local meetings and reporting problems feel small, but they are how societies work. Participate with informed choices rather than waiting for perfect leaders. Cynical withdrawal leaves space to worse ones.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, admiration, anger, argument, contempt, loyalty
related mind states: detachment

rows.description: A post of yours goes viral for the wrong reasons and thousands attack you. It is frightening and isolating. Step away from notifications, tell trusted people, save evidence of threats, report them, and do not respond in panic.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, guilt, hurt, indifference, respect
related mind states: fear, loneliness, trust

rows.description: Strangers call you names and dig up your past, and you feel worthless. Remember mobs act on fragments, not on your whole life. Correct facts once if needed, then mute; seek support, and let the storm pass.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, fear, guilt, hurt, indifference
related mind states: anger, shame

rows.description: Seeing an insulting pile-on against someone, you feel righteous and jump in. Pause: do you know the full story, and would you say it in person? Mobs do real harm; challenge wrongdoing with facts and proportion.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, fear, guilt, hurt, indifference, respect
related mind states: anger

rows.description: A stranger points out a genuine error in your work, politely. It stings, but is a gift. Thank them, fix the error and publish a correction. Owning mistakes openly makes you more credible than defensiveness.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, fear, guilt, hurt, indifference
related mind states: gratitude, admiration, anger

rows.description: After a controversy, you worry about your job and reputation. Speak with HR or a lawyer, avoid posting angry rebuttals, and consider a short, factual statement or an apology if you truly erred. Silence plus calm is often wiser.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, guilt, hurt, indifference, respect
related mind states: anger, fear, anxiety, calm
